content: The text provided is a long list of studies, trials, and publications related to HIV treatment, antiretroviral therapy, and associated conditions such as tuberculosis and pregnancy. 1. The STARTMRK study evaluated the outcomes of HIV-1-infected patients over a 156-week period, focusing on the efficacy and safety of antiretroviral regimens. 2. A randomized trial conducted in 2004 compared the efficacy and safety of tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) versus stavudine in combination therapy for antiretroviral-naive patients. 3. Long-term renal safety of tenofovir disoproxil fumarate was assessed in antiretroviral-naive HIV-1-infected patients, highlighting its tolerability and impact on kidney function. 4. A 96-week analysis compared tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, emtricitabine, and efavirenz with fixed-dose zidovudine/lamivudine and efavirenz in antiretroviral-naive patients, focusing on virologic, immunologic, and morphologic changes. 5. The SUPPORT trial evaluated cardiovascular biomarkers in a randomized study comparing fosamprenavir/ritonavir with efavirenz in underrepresented, antiretroviral-naive HIV-infected patients over 96 weeks. 6. The SWATCH study investigated the outcomes of alternating antiretroviral drug regimens for HIV infection in a randomized, controlled trial. 7. A phase IIb randomized trial assessed the efficacy and safety of TMC278 in antiretroviral-naive HIV-1 patients over a 96-week period. 8. Outcomes of non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs) in combination antiretroviral therapy were studied in adults treated in Botswana. 9. The WAVES study compared integrase inhibitor-based regimens with protease inhibitor-based regimens in HIV-1-infected women in a randomized, double-blind, phase 3 trial. 10. The ANRS 12180 Reflate TB trial evaluated the use of raltegravir for treating patients co-infected with HIV and tuberculosis in a multicenter, phase 2, non-comparative, open-label trial. 11. The ANRS 129 BKVIR trial examined the combination of tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, emtricitabine, and efavirenz in HIV-infected patients undergoing tuberculosis treatment. 12. The CARINEMO trial compared nevirapine and efavirenz in HIV and tuberculosis co-infected patients in a randomized non-inferiority trial. 13. The HIV-TB Pharmagene study explored whether efavirenz dosing should be increased during concomitant rifampicin-based tuberculosis therapy in sub-Saharan Africa. 14. The INSPIRING study assessed the safety and efficacy of dolutegravir-based antiretroviral therapy in TB/HIV co-infected adults at week 24. 15. The N2R study compared plasma drug concentrations and efficacy between two NNRTI-based regimens in HIV-infected patients receiving rifampicin. 16. Hepatotoxicity was evaluated in patients co-infected with tuberculosis and HIV-1 while receiving NNRTI-based antiretroviral therapy and rifampicin-containing anti-tuberculosis regimens. 17. A pilot study in India compared nevirapineand efavirenz-based antiretroviral therapy regimens in antiretroviral-naive patients with HIV and tuberculosis infections. 18. The MONOD-ANRS 12206 cohort studied virological responses and resistance in HIV-infected children under two years receiving lopinavir/ritonavir-based therapy in Côte d'Ivoire and Burkina Faso. 19. The PAINT trial assessed the safety and efficacy of a rilpivirine-based regimen in HIV-infected treatment-naive adolescents over 48 weeks. 20. The PROMISE trial evaluated strategies to prevent perinatal HIV transmission, including maternal antiretroviral therapy during breastfeeding. 21. The DOLPHIN-1 study compared dolutegravir and efavirenz when initiating treatment in late pregnancy. 22. The IMPAACT P1093 trial investigated the pharmacokinetics, safety, and antiviral activity of dolutegravir in HIV-infected infants, children, and adolescents. 23. The PROMOTE trial compared lopinavir/ritonavir and efavirenz-based antiretroviral therapy in HIV-infected pregnant Ugandan women, focusing on efficacy and safety. 24. The TSHEPISO study examined the pharmacokinetics of efavirenz and its use in treating HIV-1 among pregnant women with and without tuberculosis co-infection. 25. The Botswana-based study compared the safety of dolutegravir and efavirenz initiated during pregnancy, analyzing birth outcomes.
